_about: Every choice that can change a result of the analysis (requirement W2), grouped by stage: each entry its value, unit, and reason. Keys are unique across sections; the documents name them as design.KEY (tools/registry.py). Read through heidelberg/config.py. Values measured on the tuning pairs are not choices and are in heidelberg/derived.json.

geo_radius_km.reason: the radius of the geostationary orbit, at which the shadow is evaluated

danjon_parts.reason: the Earth's radius enlarged by one part in this for its atmosphere (Danjon's rule), for the shadow at its widest (which plates it can reach)

geo_trail_arcsec_s.reason: a geostationary object's motion on a sidereally guided plate, times the cosine of the declination

gaia_epoch_jyear.reason: the reference epoch of Gaia DR3's positions (J2016.0), from which stars are moved to a plate's epoch by their proper motions (Gaia Collaboration 2023)

sun_radius_km.reason: the Sun's nominal radius (IAU 2015 Resolution B3), for the share of its disc the Earth hides

shadow_instants.reason: instants spread evenly over an exposure at which the shadow is evaluated (a glint's moment is equally likely at any of them)

site_lon_deg.reason: the observing site's longitude east: Koenigstuhl, Heidelberg, within about 100 m of the observatory's published position (49 deg 23' 55" N, 8 deg 43' 15" E, 560 m); read by the shadow model, the plate times, the record set's altitudes, the estimates, the meridian search, and the asteroid ephemerides

site_lat_deg.reason: the observing site's geodetic latitude (as site_lon_deg)

pixel_arcsec.reason: the Bruce plates' scan scale (GAVO's scans), as measured on the dry run's products: median 1.020 over the 92 tuning plates' solutions, 5-95% 1.0185-1.0215 (notes/log.md, 31 October); the nominal 103 arcsec per mm is about 1% coarse

pair_start_min.reason: the two plates of a twin pair start within this of each other (the Bruce astrograph exposed both at once)

centre_sep_deg.reason: the two plates' centres lie within this (the lenses' fixed offset is 7 to 11 arcmin)

min_exposure_min.reason: both plates exposed for at least this long (the challenge's guideline is 30 minutes or more)

test_area_deg.reason: the central square of each plate in which sources are sought and the shadow is computed (21,176 px at 1.02 arcsec per pixel)

edge_lo.reason: a grid point is at the shadow's edge when in shadow for between edge_lo and edge_hi of the exposure

edge_hi.reason: a grid point is in full shadow when in shadow for at least this share of the exposure (and at the edge below it)

edge_area.reason: a pair counts as having the shadow's edge over its test area when more than this share of the area is at the edge (reported)

mostly_share.reason: a pair counts as mostly in shadow when at least this share of its test area is in full shadow (reported)

dt_share.reason: the share of pairs within which the twins' start times are reported (95%)

sep_share.reason: the central share of pairs over which the twins' centre offsets are reported (90%)

first_date.reason: the earliest exposure start in the pairing

end_before.reason: exposures starting before the launch of Sputnik 1 (4 October 1957), so before the first artificial satellite

shadow_grid_deg.reason: the grid on which a pair's shadow share is computed over the test area (cell centres)

sunlit_per_shadow.reason: sunlit pairs drawn per shadow pair, before eligibility (S7) removed some: the sunlit study (producers/sunlit_size.py, J6) gives a median expected upper limit with no glints of 0.08, 0.07, 0.06, 0.04, and 0.04 at a quarter, a half, one, two, and three per shadow pair; two is the smallest at the best limit (Donal, 1 November 2026)

match_seed.reason: the seed of the random choice of shadow pairs to match

match_dec_deg.reason: the matching's distance counts declination in units of this

match_season.reason: the matching's distance weights the month (on a circle) by this

match_year.reason: the matching's distance counts the year in units of this

examined.reason: pairs to flag and not measure; none: B7807a/B7808b, given a different selection in an earlier project, is measured like any other pair (Donal, 1 November 2026)

poss_first_year.reason: the First Palomar Sky Survey's first year of exposures (1949 to 1958): the twin pairs from then to Sputnik are counted apart

gap_min.reason: a plate whose catalogued span exceeds its net exposure by more than this is not one continuous exposure (S7)

sun_max.reason: a plate is eligible only if the Sun is below this altitude at mid-exposure (S7)

alt_min.reason: and its centre above this altitude (S7)

dateobs_tol_min.reason: GAVO's dateObs is taken to be 12 hours before the catalogue's when the two agree to within this (the sample's numbers, S5)

detect_sigma.reason: sources are detected at this many times the noise of the smoothed image (the noise measured per tile, as the grain is correlated)

detect_npix.reason: a detection covers at least this many pixels (about 10 square arcseconds)

stamp_half_px.reason: the measured stamps reach this far from each detection (heidelberg/lib/measure.py saves them; the fidelity check reads them)

smooth_sigma_px.reason: the Gaussian that smooths an image before detection (a 9-pixel kernel)

aperture_px.reason: the radius of every aperture: own, forced, and at random positions

clip_sigma.reason: sigma clipping for a noise estimate

clip_iters.reason: iterations of that clipping (for the aperture and annulus noise)

tile_px.reason: the scan is processed in square tiles of this size; the background and the detection noise are estimated per tile

tile_margin_px.reason: each tile is read with this margin and keeps only the sources whose centroid lies in its core

bkg_box_px.reason: the background is estimated in boxes of this size

bkg_filter_boxes.reason: and median-filtered over this many boxes in each direction

noise_step_px.reason: the smoothed image's noise is estimated on every this-many pixels in each direction

noise_clip_iters.reason: iterations of the sigma clipping (clip_sigma) for the detection noise

random_n.reason: random positions at which an aperture or annulus is measured for its noise

apnoise_seed.reason: the seed of the aperture noise's random positions

apnoise_margin_px.reason: those positions keep this far from the box's edges

forced_margin_px.reason: a forced measurement is made only this far inside the box

box_margin_px.reason: a position counts as inside a plate's box when at least this far from its edges

centroid_sigma_px.reason: a stamp's light centre is weighted by a Gaussian of this width

chance_zmin.reason: the chance pairs' forced measurements are made for detections at least this significant (the cut z_min is higher)

stamp_zmin.reason: stamps are kept for every detection with no Gaia star at least this significant inside both boxes (offline shape tests)

stamp_gaia_z.reason: and for Gaia stars in this range of significance

stamp_gaia_n.reason: at most this many of them, at random

stamp_seed.reason: the seed of that random choice

gaia_det_arcsec.reason: a Gaia star counts as detected when a detection lies within this (the products' Gaia table)

trail_n_bright.reason: the plate's trailing is the median axis ratio of this many brightest detections (a diagnostic)

solve_min_stars.reason: a solution is accepted with at least this many detections matched to Gaia

solve_resid_arcsec.reason: and a median match distance below this

grid_n.reason: astrometric completeness is measured in an n x n grid on the sky

grid_band.reason: from Gaia stars this far (mag) brighter than the plate's 50% G: from, to

grid_match_arcsec.reason: a Gaia star counts as detected when a detection lies within this

grid_share.reason: a solution is accepted when the median cell's completeness is at least this

grid_g_bins.reason: the plate's 50% G is found in bins of Gaia G: from, to, width

grid_min_bin.reason: a bin is used when it holds more than this many Gaia stars

grid_depth_share.reason: the 50% G: the faintest bin with at least this share of its stars detected

grid_default_g50.reason: the 50% G taken when no bin reaches that share

grid_min_cell.reason: a cell's completeness is used when it holds at least this many stars

header_alt_min.reason: a header's centre below this altitude at mid-exposure is wrong (the blind search is run)

solve_attempts.reason: the solve is tried this many times: the header's (or the blind search's) and then, if not accepted, the blind search's

gaia_width_factor.reason: the Gaia query covers the box times this

gaia_width_pad_deg.reason: plus this, plus twice the twins' separation (both boxes covered)

offset_n_det.reason: the global offset to Gaia is the peak of the offsets between this many brightest detections

offset_n_gaia.reason: and this many brightest Gaia stars

offset_half_arcsec.reason: offsets up to this in each direction

sim_scales.reason: the pre-correction also searches scales from, to (exclusive), step (some headers are 0.9% off in scale)

refine_half_arcsec.reason: the offset is refined on a grid out to this in each direction

refine_match_arcsec.reason: counting the brightest detections within this of a Gaia star

stage_n_bright.reason: the first stages of the fit use this many brightest detections

stage_gaia_g.reason: matched to Gaia stars brighter than this

solve_order.reason: the polynomial order of the final plate solution (6 deg box)

solve_stages.reason: the staged fit: per stage the match radius (arcsec), the polynomial order, and whether only the bright detections are used; the outer box is matched before the polynomial is free to bend there

inverse_span_deg.reason: the sky-to-pixel polynomial's coordinates are scaled over a square of this side

field_grid.reason: the pre-correction measures the header's error in an n x n grid of patches

field_n_det.reason: from each patch's this-many brightest detections

field_min_det.reason: a patch is used with at least this many detections

field_min_gaia.reason: and this many Gaia stars near it

field_half_arcsec.reason: offsets up to this in each direction

field_min_peak.reason: a patch's peak counts with at least this many pairs

field_peak_mask_bins.reason: and is compared with the best peak more than this many bins away

field_peak_ratio.reason: which it must exceed this many times

field_refine_bins.reason: the patch's offset is the median of the pair offsets within this many bins of the peak

field_min_patches.reason: the field is fitted with at least this many patches

field_clip_iters.reason: a quadratic is fitted with this many rounds of clipping

field_floor_arcsec.reason: plus this, so that a perfect fit does not reject every patch

field_fit_n.reason: the corrected WCS is fitted to this many detections

field_fit_seed.reason: chosen at random with this seed

field_sip_degree.reason: a TAN-SIP WCS of this degree

meridian_n_det.reason: the blind search rasterises this many brightest detections

meridian_ha_max_h.reason: over fields within this hour angle at mid-exposure

meridian_tile_deg.reason: in tangent-plane tiles of this side

meridian_dilate_px.reason: the detections' raster dilated by this many pixels

meridian_rot_deg.reason: the scan's orientation searched: from, to (exclusive), step

meridian_dec_deg.reason: tile centres in declination: from, to (exclusive), step; in RA the same step over the cosine

meridian_near_deg.reason: the Gaia stars within this of a tile's centre

meridian_min_stars.reason: a tile is searched with at least this many

meridian_gmax.reason: the blind search's all-sky Gaia list: G brighter than this (heidelberg/hd_gaia/allsky_g11.npz, pinned)

meridian_cos_floor.reason: near the pole the RA step grows as one over the cosine of the declination, capped by flooring the cosine at this

pair_radius_arcsec.reason: the two detections of a pair are each other's nearest within this

same_arcsec.reason: an original detection within this of an injection's is the same object (injections only)

n_inj.reason: artificial glints per pair (about 40 isolated star-like glints for the fidelity check)

durations.reason: the glints' durations, drawn at random

sharpen.reason: a glint's image is the local stars' shrunk by this, or not at all (a flash samples an instant)

inj_found_px.reason: a glint is found when a detection lies within this of its target

eff_g_bins.reason: the efficiency table's bins of target G: from, to, and width

eff_half.reason: the half-efficiency brightness is the faintest bin with at least this share of the peak efficiency

g_lo.reason: the artificial flashes' brightness is drawn uniformly from this star-equivalent G

g_hi.reason: to this (fainter than the plates' 50% depth near G 15, so the efficiency's fall is measured)

inj_seed.reason: the seed of the glints' positions, brightness, duration, and sharpening

inj_sep_px.reason: glints are at least this far apart

inj_tries.reason: positions are drawn until n are placed or this many times n have been tried

donor_n.reason: a glint's image is made from this many nearest donor stars

donor_pool.reason: drawn from this many times as many nearest candidates

donor_dmag.reason: within this of the glint's G

donor_bprp.reason: donors have the Sun's colour (BP - RP in this range)

donor_lone_px.reason: no other Gaia star within this

donor_margin_px.reason: and lie this far inside both boxes

donor_min.reason: a pair with fewer donors is not injected

donor_snap_px.reason: a donor is centred on its detection when one lies within this

donor_mask_a.reason: other detections in a donor's stamp are masked out to this many times their semi-major axis

donor_mask_reach.reason: out to this many stamp half-widths

donor_self_px.reason: a detection within this of the donor's centre is the donor itself

donor_outer.reason: a donor's pedestal is the median beyond this share of the stamp's half-width

donor_min_outer.reason: over at least this many unmasked pixels

donor_clip.reason: donors are combined pixel by pixel with clipping at this many robust spreads

model_noise_ring_px.reason: the model's noise is measured within this of the stamp's edge

taper_px.reason: and the model tapers to zero over this

taper_pad_px.reason: beginning this far beyond the radius at which its profile meets that noise

inj_model_g.reason: a glint's stamp half-width steps at these G

inj_model_half_px.reason: the half-widths: brighter than the first G, than the second, and fainter

inj_model_pad_px.reason: plus half the trail's length plus this

inj_dir_arcsec.reason: the plate's RA direction at a glint is measured over this

glint_spline_order.reason: a glint's image is shrunk with a spline of this order

glint_line_samples.reason: and smeared by a line sampled at this many points per pixel of its length

fid_shortfall.reason: pooled over the accepted pairs, the share of Gaia stars passing the agreement test minus the share of star-like flashes passing it may be at most this (the spec's injection fidelity criteria)

fid_axis_dex.reason: pooled, the flashes' minor axes against Gaia stars of the same brightness and colour may differ by at most this (the spec's injection fidelity criteria)

fid_noise.reason: pooled, the ratio of the flashes' image noise to their matched stars' may be at most this (the paired form) (the spec's injection fidelity criteria)

fid_pair_shortfall.reason: per pair, the agreement shortfall may be at most this plus fid_pair_sigmas counting-noise units (a gross failure only; the strict test is pooled) (the spec's injection fidelity criteria)

fid_axis_bin_dex.reason: per pair, the minor-axis offset in each G bin may be at most this plus fid_pair_sigmas standard errors (the spec's injection fidelity criteria)

fid_pair_sigmas.reason: the per-pair limits allow this many units of their own counting noise (the spec's injection fidelity criteria)

fid_min_glints.reason: a pair passes only with at least this many isolated star-like flashes (the spec's injection fidelity criteria)

fid_match_dg.reason: flashes are compared with Gaia stars within this in G (aperture significance saturates for bright sources, so it cannot be the matching variable) (the spec's injection fidelity criteria)

fid_match_k.reason: each flash is compared with its this many nearest Gaia stars in G (within fid_match_dg) (the spec's injection fidelity criteria)

fid_sun_bprp.reason: the comparison stars have the Sun's colour, BP-RP in this range, as the flashes' donor stars do (on these blue plates a red star of the same G records much fainter) (the spec's injection fidelity criteria)

fid_iso_widths.reason: flashes and stars are compared only when isolated: no other detection within this many image widths on either plate (the spec's injection fidelity criteria)

fid_gaia_match_arcsec.reason: a detection takes its Gaia G and colour from the pair's Gaia query within this; and the minor axis's comparison stars are matched to Gaia within this (the agreement's within ref_gaia_arcsec; the difference was not recorded before the restructure)

fid_axis_min_stars.reason: a flash's minor axis is compared only with at least this many Gaia stars of its G and colour on the plate

fid_axis_g_bins.reason: the G bins in which the minor-axis offset is also tested per pair (the spec's injection fidelity criteria)

fid_bin_min.reason: a G bin is tested with at least this many flashes (the spec's injection fidelity criteria)

fid_noise_inner_px.reason: the image noise is the spread in a ring from this radius to the stamp's edge, after each stamp's own azimuthal profile is removed (the spec's injection fidelity criteria)

fid_boot_n.reason: bootstrap resamples over flashes for the noise ratio's counting error

fid_pooled_sigmas.reason: the pooled fidelity criteria in equivalence form: the estimate plus this many standard errors within the limit (heidelberg/stages/summarise.py)

z_min.reason: aperture significance (flux over the spread of fluxes at random positions on the plate) required in all four measurements, own and forced on both plates; the second, simultaneous plate rejects defects, so the single-plate 30 of Solano et al. (2022) is not needed and would keep only bright sources on these plates

agree_px.reason: the agreement's differences are measured relative to stars of the same flux within these radii, in turn, then the whole plate

agree_min_stars.reason: the first radius with at least this many such stars is used

agree_pct.reason: a source passes the agreement when its distance is at most this percentile of the pair's Gaia stars'

streak_max_arcsec.reason: the longest glint streak the agreement allows (about 2 s at geostationary radius)

ratio_near_arcsec.reason: comparison stars within this of the source (800 px): each lens's vignetting differs across the plate

ratio_n_local.reason: with fewer comparison stars than this within the radius, the whole plate's are used

ratio_margin_dex.reason: allows for the two emulsions recording a brief flash differently from starlight; the stars' own ratio drifts by up to 0.25 dex with brightness across the tuning pairs (P2)

ratio_k.reason: the source's own ratio noise, in multiples, added to the margin

ratio_floor_dex.reason: the stars' scatter in ratio at high significance, added in quadrature to the source's noise

ratio_n_ref.reason: with fewer reference stars than this on the pair, no ratio is calibrated and every source passes

ratio_n_min.reason: with fewer comparison stars than this at the source's significance, the ratio is not calibrated and the source passes

ref_zmax.reason: reference stars (for the flux ratio and the elongation limit) have a significance below this; the brightest stars are left out (reason not recorded before the restructure)

elong_pct.reason: a source is point-like when its elongation is at most this percentile of its plate's Gaia stars at its flux

gaia_any_arcsec.reason: a Gaia DR3 source of any brightness within this at the plate's epoch fails gaia_any

blend_fwhm.reason: a blend: two or more Gaia stars within this many image widths

blend_dmag.reason: each brighter than the source's G-equivalent plus this

gaia_bright_g.reason: the Gaia list measured with each plate (and gaia_bright's stars) holds G brighter than this

gaia_bright_arcsec.reason: a Gaia star brighter than gaia_bright_g within this fails gaia_bright

halo_g.reason: the halo cut's radius is interpolated linearly in G through these points (none fainter than the last)

ghost_g.reason: a lens ghost: a source in a ring about a star brighter than this

ghost_r.reason: the ring's inner and outer radii

bright_g.reason: within bright_r of a star brighter than this fails the halo cut

ps1_dmag.reason: a Pan-STARRS source fails ps1 when the brighter of its PSF and Kron g is below the source's G-equivalent plus this

galaxy_arcsec.reason: an extended Pan-STARRS source within this fails the galaxy cut

galaxy_dmag.reason: extended: Kron g at least this much brighter than PSF g

galaxy_kron_g.reason: and Kron g brighter than this

var_arcsec.reason: a VSX variable or Ritter-Kolb cataclysmic binary within this fails the variable cut

sn_arcsec.reason: an Asiago supernova within this fails the variable cut

host_rmin_arcsec.reason: the supernova-host cut's radius is the larger of this

host_rfac.reason: and this many times the galaxy's K-band isophotal radius

host_kmax.reason: about 2MASS extended sources brighter than this in K (and 2MASS Large Galaxy Atlas galaxies)

ast_arcsec.reason: a source within this of a known asteroid's track over the exposure fails the asteroid cut

ast_vmax.reason: asteroids brighter than this V at the epoch

radiant_deg.reason: a source within this of an active major shower's radiant (with its daily drift) fails the meteor cut

showers.reason: the major meteor showers: name, activity start and end (month, day), peak (month, day), radiant at the peak (RA, Dec, deg), and its daily drift (deg per day in RA and Dec); International Meteor Organization calendar

validity_share.reason: a location is valid when at least this share of its nearest bright detections match Gaia, on each plate

scanner_px.reason: a source within this of a scanner mark on either plate fails scanner_mark

scanner_scans.reason: on at least this many different scans

ring_width_px.reason: the dark ring's annulus is this wide

ring_inner_fwhm.reason: its inner radius is this many times the source's FWHM

ring_random_px.reason: the ring's noise is the spread of the same mean in an annulus of these radii at random positions

ring_min.reason: a dark-ring significance below this on either plate fails dark_ring

ratio_bin_dex.reason: the comparison stars for a source's flux ratio have a geometric-mean significance within this of the source's (log10)

ref_gaia_arcsec.reason: a reference star (for the flux ratio and the elongation limit) is detected within this of its Gaia star

gaia_query_arcsec.reason: each position's Gaia query reaches beyond the 5 arcsec veto, so that a star near the veto's edge at the plate's epoch is found whatever its proper motion

ps1_arcsec.reason: a Pan-STARRS counterpart within this, as in Solano et al. (2022)

vector_zmin.reason: the two-plate sources stacked to find fixed vectors have at least this significance

vector_rmax_arcsec.reason: fixed vectors are sought out to this offset from Gaia stars

vector_star_gmax.reason: the Gaia stars whose copies are sought are brighter than this

vector_bin_arcsec.reason: offset bins of the fixed-vector stack; vectors found on both plates within one bin are one vector

vector_cut_sigma.reason: an offset bin is a fixed vector when its excess over the randomly rotated offsets exceeds this many standard deviations

vector_rotations.reason: random rotations of the offsets that give the stack's expected count (the radial profile kept)

vector_seed.reason: the seed of the random rotations

vector_min_offsets.reason: with fewer star-source offsets than this, no fixed vector is sought

vector_arcsec.reason: a source within this of a star's copy at a fixed vector is vetoed

validity_zmin.reason: the bright detections whose match to Gaia measures a solution's local validity have at least this significance

geq_bin_dex.reason: bins of log flux in which the median G of Gaia stars gives each plate's flux-to-G scale

geq_min_stars.reason: a flux bin enters the flux-to-G scale with at least this many Gaia stars

agree_pair_arcsec.reason: the agreement's calibration stars are each other's nearest detection on the two plates within this

agree_max_stars.reason: at most this many calibration stars, chosen by a hash of each star's position, so that the same stars are used whichever plate is called a

agree_flux_dex.reason: the local stars that describe an image's width and shape have a log flux within this of the image's

agree_feat_dex.reason: the calibration stars that give the expected separation and flux ratio at an image's brightness have a log flux within this of it

agree_feat_min_stars.reason: with fewer calibration stars than this at an image's brightness, its agreement is not defined and it fails

agree_min_cal.reason: with fewer calibration stars than this on the pair, the agreement cannot be calibrated and nothing passes it

agree_robust_pct.reason: the agreement's centre and covariance come from the calibration stars inside this percentile of their distance

minor_axis_pct.reason: an image's minor axis may be no wider than this percentile of the calibration stars'

elong_bin_dex.reason: bins of log flux in which the elongation limit is the stars' percentile

elong_min_stars.reason: a flux bin enters the elongation limit with at least this many stars

ps1_min_detections.reason: a Pan-STARRS source is an object with at least this many detections (the veto, and the share of random positions with a source within 5 arcsec)

drift_tail_pct.reason: the stars' ratio drift is the difference between the faintest and the brightest this-percent of the reference stars (P2)

ring_margin_px.reason: the ring is measured only this far inside the box

ring_seed.reason: the seed of the ring noise's random positions

ringnoise_margin_px.reason: those positions keep this far from the box's edges

chance_shift_arcsec.reason: the chance estimate moves one twin's detections by this, in each of the shifts' directions

shifts.reason: the chance estimate is the mean over this many shifts of one plate's detections (directions evenly spaced)

lag_radii_arcsec.reason: further shift radii at which the chance estimate is also measured: its dependence on the lag (a test, not the estimate)

alpha.reason: the level at which each test must reject for a claim

confidence.reason: the upper limit's confidence level (the belt's percentile)

null_p.reason: a null test fails if the likelihood's one-sided p-value is below this

null_tail.reason: a null test fails if either tail of the within-pair check is below this (the check two-sided at null_p)

inj_finals.reason: the injection null uses at most this many passing injections per pair as its finals, in both tests

null_shares.reason: the glint shares (of surviving sources) over which the composite null's p-value is the largest

candidate_toys.reason: toy record sets per glint share for the candidates' p-value

check_draws.reason: draws of control positions for the within-pair check's null distribution

belt_toys.reason: toy record sets per glint share in the upper limit's belt

shrink_chance_parts.reason: each pair's toy background is (k c_i + c_mean) / (k + 1) with k this, c_mean the mean chance estimate over the sample's pairs

b_lo.reason: each pair's background in the likelihood is bounded below by this (per pair)

b_hi.reason: and above by this (per pair; the tuning pairs' chance estimates are near 1)

kappa_lo.reason: the suppression in shadow kappa is fitted within kappa_lo to kappa_hi

kappa_hi.reason: kappa = 1: glints vanish in full shadow

bruehl_n.reason: random positions per pair in Bruehl et al.'s test as published

shadow_split.reason: a surviving source counts as in shadow, in the per-pair table, above this shadow share

fit_eta_start.reason: the fit's starting glint density per pair, and the floor of each background's starting value

fit_kappa_starts.reason: the fit with kappa free starts from each of these and keeps the best (the likelihood can have more than one minimum)

newton_iter.reason: the most Newton steps that profile each background (they converge in far fewer)

newton_step.reason: the largest Newton step in ln B

grad_xatol.reason: the map's fit: Nelder-Mead's tolerance on the gradient

grad_fatol.reason: the map's fit: Nelder-Mead's tolerance on -ln L

ul_xatol.reason: the upper limit's search for eta hat: its tolerance

ul_eta_min.reason: the upper limit's search for eta hat starts above this (per pair)

ul_eta_max_factor.reason: and ends at this many reference backgrounds

null_toys.reason: toy record sets per glint share for each null test's likelihood p-value

belt_grid.reason: the glint shares at which the upper limit's Neyman belt is computed

toy_b_min.reason: a pair's toy background is at least this

grad_boot.reason: bootstrap resamples over pairs for the map's uncertainty

seed_inj_finals.reason: the seed choosing the injection null's finals

seed_check.reason: the seed of the within-pair check's draws

seed_deficit.reason: the seed of the positive control's thinning: each flash kept with probability one minus its shadow share

seed_grad_boot.reason: the seed of the map's bootstrap

seed_bruehl.reason: the seed choosing Bruehl et al.'s random positions

seed_toys.reason: the seed of the likelihood's and the belt's toys

summary_boot.reason: bootstrap resamples over pairs for the summary's chance background error

overdispersion_boot.reason: bootstrap resamples over the tuning pairs for the overdispersion's standard error (heidelberg/stages/derived.py)

role_rule.reason: no claim if shadow and sunlit pairs differ by more than this standardised difference in acceptance, selection, depth, aperture noise, or efficiency

offset_report_deg.reason: part one reports, by role, the pairs whose solved centre lies further than this from GAVO's (S8)

time_consistent_min.reason: a plate's times are self-consistent when GAVO's mid-exposure lies within this of its start plus half its exposure (reported by role)

bracket_lo.reason: a brief flash records brighter than a star of the same energy (reciprocity failure): at least this many magnitudes, a systematic in the rate

rec_plates.reason: recurrence: up to this many other Bruce plates per location, the longest exposures

rec_blank.reason: recurrence: blank positions per pair (introduced flashes' positions), against which the candidates' rate is read

rec_min_days.reason: recurrence: the other plates are more than this many days from the pair

rec_blank_seed.reason: the seed choosing each pair's blank positions

rec_cutout_deg.reason: the radius of each GAVO cut-out

rec_cutout_min_px.reason: a cut-out narrower than this (square) is not measured

rec_bg_box_px.reason: the cut-out's background is estimated in boxes of this size

rec_bg_filter_px.reason: and filtered over this many boxes

rec_detect_npix.reason: a detection on a cut-out covers at least this many pixels (the measurement asks 10 on the whole plate; the difference was not recorded before the restructure)

rec_gaia_margin.reason: the pair's Gaia stars within this many cut-out radii enter the local solve

rec_edge_px.reason: and lie at least this far inside the cut-out

rec_min_stars.reason: a cut-out is solved only with at least this many Gaia stars and detections

rec_n_bright.reason: the brightest detections and Gaia stars that find the offset

rec_angles_deg.reason: the rotations searched (from, to, step), each parity, and a half turn (a plate scanned the other way)

rec_offset_bins.reason: in this many bins each way

rec_match_px.reason: the affine solve's match radii, in turn

rec_min_matches.reason: a solve needs at least this many matches at each radius

rec_margin_px.reason: the location, and the random noise apertures, lie at least this far inside the cut-out

rec_noise_n.reason: random apertures that give the cut-out's aperture noise

rec_z_hit.reason: a location is recorded on a plate when its forced significance is at least this

rec_zexp_min.reason: a plate is informative when a static source of the location's G would reach this significance on it

rec_hits_min.reason: a location is recurrent when recorded on at least this many informative plates (or on the only one)

rec_depth_bin_mag.reason: a plate's local depth: the median log significance of Gaia stars in bins of this width in G

rec_depth_min_stars.reason: a bin enters with at least this many stars

rec_depth_min_bins.reason: the depth is defined with at least this many bins

rec_z_floor.reason: significances below this count as this (logarithms)

clock_min_stars.reason: the clock's rule: the cut-out's astrometric fit has at least this many Gaia stars

clock_across_arcsec.reason: the trail lies within this of the predicted track

clock_length.reason: its measured length is this range of times the predicted motion over the exposure

clock_band_min.reason: plates whose offset lies in this range of minutes are reported

clock_far_min.reason: plates off by more than this many minutes are reported

clock_offset_sigmas.reason: part one shifts every plate time by the asteroid clock's median offset on the main sample's plates when it differs from zero by more than this many standard errors (and by more than clock_correct_min; stages/clock_correct.py) (Donal, 1 November 2026)

clock_correct_min.reason: and by more than this many minutes: smaller offsets move the shadow by less than about 0.15 degrees (a 25-minute error moves it about 0.7)

clock_boot.reason: bootstrap resamples over plates for the median offset's standard error

clock_vmax.reason: asteroids predicted brighter than this V time the plate

clock_gaia_gmax.reason: the cut-out's astrometric fit uses Gaia stars brighter than this

clock_cutout_half_px.reason: the cut-out around each asteroid reaches this far each way

clock_gaia_margin.reason: Gaia stars within this many cut-out half-widths (arcsec per pixel, times the square root of two, rounded up) enter the fit

clock_bg_box_px.reason: the cut-out's background is estimated in boxes of this size

clock_bg_filter_px.reason: and filtered over this many boxes

clock_n_bright.reason: the brightest detections that find the cut-out's offset

clock_offset_bins.reason: in this many bins each way

clock_match_arcsec.reason: the affine fit's match radii, in turn

clock_search_across_arcsec.reason: segments within this of the predicted track are measured (the rule then asks clock_across_arcsec)

clock_search_along_arcsec.reason: and within the predicted length plus this along it

clock_end_pct.reason: a segment's ends are these percentiles of its pixels along the track

clock_error_min.reason: an estimate: the shadow's displacement for a clock error of this many minutes

opposition_deg.reason: an estimate: asteroids' motion within this of opposition

est_h.reason: an estimate: an asteroid at the ephemeris veto's limit (H = 15) ...

est_r_au.reason: ... at the main belt's inner edge from the Sun ...

est_delta_au.reason: ... and this far from Earth, at opposition: its V

est_a_au.reason: an estimate: a main-belt asteroid's circular, coplanar orbit, for its motion over an exposure

est_meteor_path_km.reason: an estimate: a meteor's luminous path ...

est_image_arcsec.reason: ... leaves a point image only if projected within an image's width

parallax_share.reason: the parallax range stated covers this share of the record pairs (central)

ps1_positions.reason: random positions per tuning field for the share with a Pan-STARRS source within the counterpart radius (N4)

drand_round.reason: the drand quicknet round at the registered unlock (unlock_utc); R4 derives it from drand's genesis and period

unlock_utc.reason: the registered unlock: the sealed results open at drand's round for this time (drand_round)

deadline_utc.reason: the unlock must lie after the pre-registration deadline (the end of 15 January 2027)

select_lead_s.reason: part one locks the selection's workspace to a time at least this far ahead

dry_lead_s.reason: in the dry run, both locks are to a round this far ahead

label_swap_pairs.reason: the tuning pairs on which D5 exchanges plates a and b (tests/label_swap_real.py)

replica_min_days.reason: a replica moves a plate to another night at least this many days from its own (the shadow moves about 1 degree a day)

replica_max_days.reason: and at most this many (half a year either way)

control_n_drawn.reason: record pairs drawn at random, in order, until this many have a different-night partner (before eligibility, S7, removed some)

control_seed.reason: the seed of that random order

control_sep_deg.reason: the different-night plate's centre lies within this of plate a's (the same field)

control_min_days.reason: the two plates are from different nights: more than this apart

power_toys.reason: toy record sets per case for the power table, the claim rule's size, and the robustness

cal_null_toys.reason: toy record sets per glint share for the critical value (16,000: its 95th percentile to about 0.08; 4,000 gave 0.16, and the largest over shares picked a high fluctuation)

cal_belt_toys.reason: toy record sets per glint share for the belt's expected limit and coverage

cal_q95_boot.reason: bootstrap resamples for each critical value's standard error

cal_bg_gamma_shape.reason: each toy pair's background is drawn from a gamma distribution of this shape about the tuning background (a coefficient of variation of 0.5)

cal_check_draws.reason: draws for the within-pair check in each power toy

cal_seed_null.reason: the seed of the null toys (with the share and the toy's number)

cal_seed_power.reason: the seed of the power toys

cal_seed_limit.reason: the seed of the belt's toys

cal_seed_robust.reason: the seed of the robustness toys

cal_unsuppressed_shares.reason: glint shares present but not suppressed in shadow, at which the likelihood's false rejection is reported

cal_power_shares.reason: the glint shares of the power table

cal_power_kappas.reason: the suppressions in shadow of the power table

cal_size_shares.reason: the glint shares (unsuppressed) at which the claim rule's and the within-pair test's false rejections are reported, for each map case; 0.5, the largest null share, also stands for static sources (uniform and unsuppressed, as such glints are) at about 1.2 per pair against the tuning background

cal_map_cases.reason: the true background map in the size cases, as a multiple of the fitted gradient (the fit always uses the fitted one)

cal_shadow_heavy.reason: robustness: a pair whose mean shadow share exceeds this has the lower glint efficiency in the efficiency case

value: centre-heavy a = -0.64 (the tuning set's measured profile)
glints f 0.25 unsuppressed, efficiency 0.8 on shadow pairs: unweighted fit
the same, fit weighted by each pair's efficiency
background map half the fitted gradient
background map 1.5 x the fitted gradient
static 1.2 per pair (above the different-night bound)
cal_robust_cases.reason: the likelihood's robustness cases: each a way the toys' truth departs from the fit's model (overdispersion, static sources, a radial background, unsuppressed glints with lower efficiency in shadow, the map's gradient)

cal_coverage_shares.reason: the glint shares at which the belt's expected limit (0) and its coverage are computed

cal_chance_scales.reason: factors on every chance estimate at which the limit is recomputed against the same belt: the tuning pairs check the chance estimate's scale only to about 17% (33 surviving sources against 33.6), and 10% either way shows how the limit leans on it

cal_blur_sets.reason: geometry sets with the plate times in error as the asteroid clock found them, used in turn by the blurred toys; ten draws of 881 pair offsets from the clock's 19 tuning plates

cal_seed_blur.reason: the seed of the blurred geometry sets' offsets

cal_sunlit_cases.reason: the sunlit pairs per shadow pair compared by the sunlit study (producers/sunlit_size.py): a quarter is about the 113 drawn first; three and four show where the gain levels off (Donal, 1 November 2026)

cal_sunlit_null_toys.reason: toy record sets for each case's critical value in the sunlit study (its 95th percentile to about 0.16, enough to rank the cases)

cal_sunlit_toys.reason: toy record sets per power case and per belt share in the sunlit study

cal_pooled_toys.reason: toy record sets for the pooled test's false rejection (J4; the stamp has used 2,000, passed by the pipeline, though the script's default was 4,000)

cal_pooled_slope.reason: the pooled test's second case: the background falls by this fraction across the pairs' mean shadow shares

cal_seed_pooled.reason: the seeds of the pooled test's two cases

vsx_field_deg.reason: VSX is fetched within this of a record-set pair's GAVO centre (the test area's half-diagonal, 4.2 deg, and a margin for GAVO's centre)

vsx_margin_deg.reason: or, for measured pairs, out to the test area's farthest detection plus this

vsx_field_wide_deg.reason: record fields whose a-plate lies in the range where GAVO's centres are often wrong (facts: gavo_wrong_centres) are fetched this wide: 1.3 deg beyond the test area's half-diagonal, against 0.16 at vsx_field_deg

storage_months.reason: the measured products are stored for the project's nine months and a three-month margin

calibration_runs.reason: the calibration's runs counted in the budget (the stamped calibration and reruns)

storage_read_months.reason: the products are read in the first three months (part two and the report), so each stays in Intelligent-Tiering's frequent tier until 30 days after that

bg_seed.reason: the seed of the backgrounds' random rotations and positions

bg_zmin.reason: the backgrounds use two-plate sources with no Gaia star at least this significant

bg_gaia_g.reason: fixed-offset copies: offsets from Gaia stars brighter than this

bg_offset_bins.reason: histogrammed in this many bins in each direction

bg_min_offsets.reason: on pairs with more than this many offsets

bg_rotations.reason: against this many random rotations of the same offsets

bg_peak_z.reason: a bin is reported when its excess is above this

ghost_star_g.reason: lens ghosts: reflections of stars brighter than this

ghost_star_arcsec.reason: located by their nearest detection within this

ghost_scale.reason: reflected about the plate centre at scales from, to (exclusive), step

ghost_r_px.reason: sources counted within this of a reflection

mark_zmin.reason: scanner marks: sharp single-plate sources with no Gaia star at least this significant

mark_r_px.reason: recurring within this at the same scan pixel

ephem_hmax.reason: orbits of asteroids with H at most this are integrated (the asteroid veto's catalogue)

ephem_field_deg.reason: asteroids are kept within this of a plate's centre (as SkyBoT's cone)

ephem_margin_deg.reason: plus this margin, so that a small change of a plate's time or centre needs no new integration

ephem_kepler_iter.reason: Newton iterations of Kepler's equation for the initial states

delta_t.reason: TT - UT taken as c0 + c1 (year - c2): a linear approximation near 1950; about 8 s too large in 1905, which moves an asteroid by under a tenth of an arcsecond
